A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison. The regression analysis moved from v2's main text is identifiable in v3's Appendix K.

before.justification: v2 reports original SAE experiments, language-model task accuracies, activation interventions, and regression analyses, including supplementary results in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds SAE-plane intervention comparisons, clustering sensitivity tests, and analyses of ranked feature clusters.

M1.justification: Section 5.2 adds an intervention variant that fits the circular probe within the plane discovered by SAE clustering, instead of the task activation's top-five-PCA subspace. The underlying SAE training, clustering, irreducibility tests, and regression method are retained. Algorithm 1 documents the existing discovery procedure.

E1.justification: The training corpora, synthetic feature distributions, Weekdays and Months tasks, and continuity prompts retain their coverage. New cluster analyses reuse existing activations, while transferring probes across layers changes experimental settings rather than data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The new Section 5.2 comparison evaluates the SAE-plane probe against per-layer circular probes and a circular probe fitted at layer 8 and transferred to adjacent layers. The original full-layer, PCA-subspace, average-ablation, and no-operation comparisons in Figure 6 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols fit a probe at layer 8 and evaluate it across layers 6–10, sweep clustering parameters k and the similarity cutoff, and assess cluster stability using Jaccard similarity. Composite cluster-ranking rules are also introduced. Existing task sample sizes, accuracy evaluation, and intervention protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends validation with direct interventions in the automatically discovered SAE plane, transfer tests across layers, clustering-parameter sensitivity in Appendix F.2, and current-token versus next-token cluster analyses in Appendix G. These address causal relevance, robustness, and interpretation of discovered features. The earlier EVR analyses remain in Appendix K.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 96% normal-approximation confidence intervals across prompt-level intervention effects, with the same 294 Weekdays and 1,584 Months interventions. Existing patching run counts and toy-experiment seed annotations are retained. No changed uncertainty estimator, significance test, or repeated-run policy is documented.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantive intervention, stability, and cluster-ranking results. Section 5.2 reports layer-6 transfer effects of -2.32 for the SAE probe versus 0.029 for the ordinary layer-8 probe. Figure 10(a) also changes the mixture index from 0.3621 to 0.6396 and separability index from 0.7907 to 0.3691. Tables 1–4 retain their results; these additions are not task-accuracy improvements.

T1.justification: Hypothesis 2 removes v2's requirement that every subset of features be mutually independent on its shared domain, deleting a strong constraint from the central formal hypothesis. Adjacent prose still asserts independence, leaving an inconsistency. The capacity theorem and proofs in Appendix A and alternative definitions in Appendix C are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that irreducible multidimensional features exist, SAE clustering can discover them, and circular representations participate causally in modular arithmetic. The revised title clarifies the already stated one-dimensional meaning of linearity. EVR loses headline prominence, but its findings remain in Appendix K rather than being withdrawn.

C2.justification: v3 adds a cone/intensity interpretation of the circular features and suggests that transfer robustness indicates more intrinsic SAE-discovered features. Its limitations now emphasize statistical rather than intervention-based definitions, subjective reducibility scores, and possibly higher-dimensional undiscovered features. It removes the explicit failed-clock-circuit and maximum-8B-model caveats from the discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds high-level discovery pseudocode, and Section 5.2 specifies the SAE plane, probe fitting, and transfer setup. New ranking and sensitivity analyses receive procedural details. Existing SAE hyperparameters, hardware, training times, software, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of Shai et al.'s belief-state geometry, cites Belrose et al. for neighboring-layer representations, and adds Kantamneni and Tegmark to the linearity discussion. Huh et al. is removed with the speculation about universality at larger model sizes. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The title becomes more precise, several method explanations and limitations are rewritten, and the former Section 5.2 EVR material is consolidated into Appendix K. New appendix subdivisions organize the added analyses. These are localized revisions within a largely retained document structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial visual material: intervention-transfer curves, clustering-stability heatmaps, a large ranked-cluster panel, and an SAE-plane projection. The earlier EVR circle moves from Figure 8 to Figure 23. Existing displays receive clearer captions and annotations, and Figure 10(a) is redrawn; the tables retain their structure.

improvement.justification: The SAE-plane interventions strengthen the connection between automatic feature discovery and causal computation, while sensitivity tests and ranked-cluster displays make the evidence more transparent. These are useful gains within the existing experimental scope. The unreconciled independence statement surrounding Hypothesis 2 limits theoretical clarity, so the overall improvement is modest.
